post.caption: Under five dollars in three days. That was the first sales total of Tiffany and Young, a shop that Charles Lewis Tiffany and John B. Young opened at 259 Broadway in New York in September 1837. Tiffany was 25, and his father lent them 1,000 dollars to start. The shop sold stationery and fancy goods, such as fans and umbrellas, at fixed prices. In 1853, it became Tiffany and Company. In 1858, Tiffany bought 20 miles of leftover Atlantic telegraph cable and sold pieces of it as souvenirs.
